newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU deal on leg-hold traps is "a con" - Pimenta.
newsitem.headline: EU deal on leg-hold traps is "a con" - Pimenta.

text.p: A leading European Parliament campaigner slammed European Union foreign ministers on Tuesday for endorsing a draft deal with Canada and Russia on more humane standards for trapping animals for their fur.
"I am very disappointed," Portuguese Christian Democrat Carlos Pimenta told Reuters. "It is a con."

Pimenta, who has spearheaded a campaign by parliament and animal welfare groups to outlaw the steel-jawed leg-hold trap, attacked the ministers for introducing changes to the draft EU deal which he said fundamentally weaken the accord.

Earlier versions of the text, drafted by the European Commission, set a four-year deadline for outlawing the traps, which do not kill animals outright but often break their legs and imprison them until they bleed or starve to death.

But the ministers on Monday rejected the idea of a fixed deadline and agreed instead that countries signing up to the international accord should be allowed to produce unilateral declarations saying when they intended to stop using the traps.

Pimenta said the move was designed to get another major fur exporter, the United States, to sign up to the deal and lift its threat to impose trade sanctions if the EU enforced its long- delayed ban on imports of fur from animals caught in the traps.

"It is a loophole which means that any new party -- and we're talking about the U.S. -- can sign the convention and then say they will (ban leg-hold traps) whenever they like. It has no teeth whatsoever," said Pimenta.
A US official said Washington was continuing talks with Brussels but still felt unable to accept the deal as it stood.
"I think the agreement Canada and Russia have helps us in some regard but it's not something we can sign up to," the official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
The US did not accept that leg-hold traps were necessarily inhumane and should be banned, he said.

Pimenta said the deal with Canada and Russia was deeply flawed on a second count, in that its definition of "humane" trapping standards was based on the assumption that traps could be selective and that an underwater trap designed to catch otters would not also catch and drown other species.

The European Parliament is due on June 12 to adopt a motion drafted by Pimenta vehemently criticising the draft agreement, in a move designed to put pressure on EU environment ministers who will have the final say on June 19-20.
If the parliament fails to persuade the ministers not to accept the deal, it may still have a chance to cause trouble when the accord is transposed into EU law.
Parliament has joint power with ministers to approve or reject that piece of internal EU legislation.
